# Mobile System Design Interview

> System design for iOS and Android engineers: offline sync, caching, push, performance, and eight question walkthroughs. A free guide from DesignGurus.io, in plain Markdown, with no account required.

Each page is short and ends with links to full course lessons and free articles. Each description below is the opening sentence of that page.

## Guide pages

- [The Five-Step Method for a Mobile System Design Round](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/framework.md): A mobile design round should be spent in five steps, in this order: requirements, API and data model, client architecture, deep dive, then failure and shipping.

## Cheat sheets

- [Common Mistakes in the Mobile System Design Round](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/common-mistakes.md): Most candidates who fail this round do not fail on knowledge.
- [Four-Week Plan for the Mobile System Design Interview](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/four-week-plan.md): This plan takes about six hours a week for four weeks, which is 24 hours in total.
- [iOS vs Android Differences](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/ios-vs-android-differences.md): The method for a mobile design round is the same on both platforms, and most of the design is shared.
- [Mobile vs Backend System Design](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/mobile-vs-backend-system-design.md): In a backend round the candidate designs the servers behind a product.
- [Mobile System Design Question Bank](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/cheat-sheets/question-bank.md): This page lists 40 questions that are commonly reported from mobile system design rounds for iOS and Android roles.

## Concepts

- [App Architecture Layers](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/concepts/app-architecture-layers.md): A mobile application is usually divided into four layers: UI, presentation, domain, and data.
- [App Performance](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/concepts/app-performance.md): Mobile performance comes down to four measurements: how fast the app starts, how smoothly it scrolls, how much memory it holds, and how large it is to download.
- [Background Work and Battery](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/concepts/background-work-and-battery.md): Once an app leaves the screen, the operating system decides whether its code runs at all.
- [Image Loading and Caching](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/concepts/image-loading-and-caching.md): An image pipeline has four jobs: fetch the right size, cache it at two levels, decode it off the main thread, and cancel work for rows that have scrolled away.
- [Local Storage](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/concepts/local-storage.md): A mobile app has five kinds of on-device storage, and a good design names which data goes in which.
- [Networking and API Contracts](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/concepts/networking-and-api-contracts.md): A mobile client needs an API that is small per response, safe to retry, and tolerant of old app versions.
- [Offline-First and Sync](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/concepts/offline-first-and-sync.md): An offline-first app treats the local store as the source of truth: every screen reads from the device, and the network is only a way to bring that store up to date.
- [Pagination and Feeds](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/concepts/pagination-and-feeds.md): Pagination is the practice of loading a long list in pages instead of all at once.
- [Push Notifications](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/concepts/push-notifications.md): A push notification is a message that reaches a device through a connection the operating system keeps open for all apps.
- [Real-Time Updates](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/concepts/real-time-updates.md): A mobile app has five ways to learn that something changed on the server: polling, long polling, server-sent events, WebSockets, and push notifications.
- [Release and Feature Flags](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/concepts/release-and-feature-flags.md): A mobile release cannot be taken back.
- [Security and Privacy](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/concepts/security-and-privacy.md): Mobile security starts from one assumption: the device and the app are in the hands of the attacker.

## Questions

- [Design a Chat App](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/questions/design-a-chat-app.md): A chat client shows a list of conversations and, inside each one, a stream of messages that arrive in real time.
- [Design a Maps and Location App](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/questions/design-a-maps-and-location-app.md): A maps client draws a map the user can pan and zoom, shows the user's position on it, and searches for places.
- [Design a Mobile Payments Flow](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/questions/design-a-mobile-payments-flow.md): In this question the user sends money to another person or pays for an order from the app.
- [Design a News Feed App](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/questions/design-a-news-feed-app.md): The feed is the most common mobile design question.
- [Design a Photo Sharing App](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/questions/design-a-photo-sharing-app.md): In this question the user picks a photo, adds a caption, and posts it for others to see.
- [Design a Ride Hailing App](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/questions/design-a-ride-hailing-app.md): A ride hailing product has two apps: one for riders and one for drivers.
- [Design a Video Streaming App](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/questions/design-a-video-streaming-app.md): A video client plays content that is far too large to download before playback begins.
- [Design an Offline Notes App](https://github.com/design-gurus/mobile-system-design-interview/blob/main/questions/design-an-offline-notes-app.md): A notes app must work fully without a network: the user creates, edits, and deletes notes on a plane, and the changes reach their other devices later.
